extracted.intended_audience: Authors, printers, designers, sculptors, proprietors, and legal practitioners seeking to secure or enforce statutory rights in the United Kingdom (late 18th–early 19th century).
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts statutory standards governing exclusive rights, formalities, remedies, penalties, deposit/registration and limitation periods for printed patterns, sculptures/models/casts, and books under several late-18th/early-19th century UK Acts. Useful for determining who obtains protection, required formalities, enforcement remedies, and time limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusive right for new and original printed patterns (linens, cottons, calicoes, muslins)
rubrics_metrics.description: From and after the first day of July 1794, every person who shall invent, design, and print, or cause to be invented, designed, and printed, and become the proprietor of any new and original pattern or patterns for printing linens, cottons, calicoes, or muslins, shall have the sole right and liberty of printing and reprinting the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Term to commence from day of first publishing; each piece shall be truly printed with the name of the printer or proprietors at each end; unauthorized printing/working/copying/publishing/sale of such patterns without the proprietor's written consent (signed in presence of two or more credible witnesses) and with knowledge that the work is unauthorized is actionable in a special action upon the case to recover damages and costs (no wager of law, essoin, privilege, protection, or more than one imparlance allowed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Term of protection for printed patterns
rubrics_metrics.description: The sole right and liberty of printing and reprinting new and original patterns for specified textiles shall subsist for the term of three months to commence from the day of the first publishing thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The three-month term is measured from first publication; statutory marking (name of printer/proprietors at each end) is a precondition for protection/enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sole right/property in new models and casts (sculpture, busts, statues, casts from nature)
rubrics_metrics.description: From the passing of the Act (38 Geo. III c.71), every person who shall make or cause to be made any new model, or copy or cast made from such new model (of busts, statues, human/animal figures, alto or basso relievo, or casts from nature) shall have the sole right and property in every such new model, copy, or cast for the term of fourteen years from the time of first publishing the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proprietor must cause his or her name, with the date of the publication, to be put thereon before publication; the fourteen-year term is the statutory monopoly period for such sculptural works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on unauthorized copies/imports/sales of models/casts and formal consent requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person who, within the fourteen-year term, shall make or cause to be made, import, sell, or otherwise dispose of any copy or cast of any such new model, copy, or cast without the express consent of the proprietor first had and obtained in writing signed in the presence of and attested by two or more credible witnesses, shall be liable to action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proprietors may bring a special action upon the case against offenders and recover such damages as a jury shall assess together with full costs of suit; the statute lists the specified prohibited acts (making, causing, importing, selling, exposing to sale, or procuring) and requires written witnessed consent to permit others to deal in the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purchaser/assignee protection for models/casts
rubrics_metrics.description: No person who shall hereafter purchase the right, either in any such model, copy, or cast, or in any such work from the original proprietor, shall be subject to any action for vending or selling any cast or copy from the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A bona fide purchaser of the statutory right from the original proprietor is protected against actions for vending/selling copies derived from that work (i.e., assignment transfers the defensible title to deal in the work).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation period for actions under the models/casts Act
rubrics_metrics.description: All actions to be brought against any person or persons for any offence committed against the Act shall be commenced within six calendar months next after the discovery of every such offence, and not afterwards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an action is not commenced within six months after discovery, it is barred; this short limitation is a procedural precondition to enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors' statutory copyright in books (14-year initial term)
rubrics_metrics.description: The author of any book already composed and not printed or published, and the author of any book which shall hereafter be composed (and their assigns), shall have the sole liberty of printing and reprinting such book or books for the term of fourteen years to commence from the day of first publishing the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Right vests in authors (and assignees); statutory initial term is fourteen years from first publication; the Act contemplates a second term in certain circumstances (see separate entry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Second 14-year term for books if author still living
rubrics_metrics.description: After the expiration of the said term of fourteen years, the right of printing or disposing of copies shall return to the authors thereof, if they are then living, for another term of fourteen years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides statutory renewal/extension where the author survives the initial statutory term; the continuation is conditional on the author being alive at the end of the first term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formalities and entry in register of the Company of Stationers (books)
rubrics_metrics.description: The right and title of the proprietor or proprietors (other than certain college bequests) must be duly entered in the register book of the Company of Stationers in London in the usual manner; consent for printing/reprinting/importing/selling should likewise be entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to enter rights/consents in the register (or to enter the college's rights by specified deadlines) can prevent reliance on statutory remedies; clerk of the Stationers shall give certificates of entries, make half-yearly lists for Trinity College, and may take modest fees; refusal or neglect by the clerk to register or certify (after notice) exposes the clerk to forfeiture (£20) and parties may obtain constructive benefit by advertisement if clerk refuses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deposit/duplicate-copy obligations for printed books
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to the copies required by law to be delivered to the warehouse-keeper of the Company of Stationers, one other copy shall be delivered for the use of the library of Trinity College Dublin and one other copy for the use of the library of the Society of the King's Inns, Dublin, by the printer or printers of books entered in the register book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These deposit obligations are enforceable with penalties for default analogous to existing delivery penalties; they create statutory obligations to provide library copies for specified institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on Trinity College Dublin's perpetual rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Trinity College Dublin shall for ever have the sole right of printing books given or bequeathed to them unless they are given for a limited time only; provided the college prints such books at their own press within the college and for its sole benefit; if the college delegates, grants, leases, or sells the copyrights or allows others to print, the privilege becomes void.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The perpetual privilege is conditional on internal printing and exclusive benefit; delegation or alienation of the printing/copyrights voids the extraordinary privilege.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on importing books first composed in the United Kingdom and reprinted abroad
rubrics_metrics.description: It shall not be lawful to import into any part of the United Kingdom for sale any printed book or books first composed, written, or printed and published in the United Kingdom and reprinted in any other country; any such imported book shall be forfeited and made waste paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offenders shall also forfeit £10 and double the value of each copy; books may be seized by officers of customs or excise who may be rewarded up to the value of the books; exceptions exist (e.g., books not printed/reprinted in the UK within twenty years prior to import or certain collections where greatest part composed abroad).

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalties, forfeitures and enforcement remedies for unauthorized books
rubrics_metrics.description: Offenders against the books provisions are liable to special action at the suit of the proprietor to recover damages, double costs of suit, forfeiture of the book(s) and sheets, and a penalty of threepence per sheet (and in import cases, £10 plus double the value). Courts may order delivery of seized copies to the proprietor; customs/excise officers may seize and be rewarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remedies include civil actions for damages and costs, statutory forfeiture of infringing copies (made waste), monetary penalties per sheet, and enforcement via courts and customs/excise; certain procedural constraints (no wager of law, essoin, privilege, and limited imparlances) apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actions brought under these Acts: defendant's general issue plea and costs
rubrics_metrics.description: If an action or suit is commenced against any person for doing anything in pursuance of the Act, defendants may plead the general issue and give special matter in evidence; if a verdict is for the defendant or the plaintiff becomes nonsuited or discontinues, the defendant shall have and recover his full costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides procedural protection to persons acting under the statute and a costs-shifting rule when defendant prevails; actions for offences under these Acts must generally be brought within six months or be void.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension/continuance of rights for works previously published under earlier Acts
rubrics_metrics.description: The sole right and property of all works which have been put forth or published under the protection of the earlier recited Act shall be extended, continued to and vested in the respective proprietors for the term of fourteen years to commence from the date when such works respectively were put forth or published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision preserves and extends protection for works already published under prior legislation, effectively renewing or confirming proprietors' exclusive rights for a fresh statutory term.
